source.check: returned unopposed: no contest in the division (Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 6 May 1939, p. 2); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Ballymena Observer, 4 August 1939, p. 2: 'David Foster' present; Ballymena Observer, 15 September 1939, p. 3: sympathy on the death of Mr. Foster, 'the member for Ballyclug, who had been a member of the Board for a considerable number of years')

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, June 1939 (statutory day Thursday 1 June 1939): no contest. The Ballymena Observer of 5 May 1939, p. 10, lists the twelve divisions with one nomination, all 'old members of the Council', and the eleven in which 'the following retiring members were deemed re-elected'. Twenty divisions are corroborated by the council's meetings of June-September 1939 (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026); Ballyscullion, Drumanaway and Newtowncrommelin are taken from the deemed list. No party labels are printed. division inferred from the 1 June 1933 return (David Foster; Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1933, p. 10); the Ballymena Observer, 4 August 1939, p. 2 names the member as sitting for the new council (meeting of the Ballymena Board of Guardians, Saturday 29 July 1939). He died in September 1939, three months into the term; his successor is not traced here. Returned unopposed.
